question: Shadows are formed when __________ objects come in the path of light.
solution:
The correct answer is __**opaque**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Opaque objects** are those that do not allow light to pass through them.
 
• When light encounters an opaque object, it is either absorbed or reflected, but not transmitted.
 
• This interaction of light with opaque objects results in the formation of **shadows**.
 
• Shadows are areas where light is blocked by the opaque object, creating a dark shape on a surface opposite the light source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Luminous objects** are those that emit their own light, such as the sun or a light bulb.
 
• **Transparent objects** allow light to pass through them completely, like clear glass or clean water.
 
• **Translucent objects** allow some light to pass through but scatter it, such as frosted glass or thin paper.
 
• The study of light and shadows is a fundamental aspect of physics, specifically in the branch of optics.
